payload.task_text:
You are a financial analyst conducting a financial health assessment of tracked companies. Your workspace contains no pre-existing files for this task.

Connect to the Yahoo Finance data source and retrieve the financial statement data for the available tracked stocks. You need income statement data (total revenue, net income) and balance sheet data (total assets, total liabilities, stockholders equity) for each company from the most recent annual period.

Create an Excel file called Financial_Health_Report.xlsx in your workspace with two sheets. The first sheet should be called "Income Statement" with columns: Symbol, Total_Revenue, Net_Income, Profit_Margin_Pct (which is Net_Income divided by Total_Revenue times 100, rounded to 1 decimal place). Include rows for each of the five stocks: AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM, and XOM. Sort the rows alphabetically by Symbol.

The second sheet should be called "Balance Sheet" with columns: Symbol, Total_Assets, Total_Liabilities, Equity. Populate it with the corresponding balance sheet data for the same five stocks, sorted alphabetically by Symbol.

Create a Notion page titled "Financial Health Dashboard" that summarizes the key findings from your analysis. The page should mention which companies have the highest revenue, best profit margins, and strongest balance sheets based on the data you retrieved.

Send an email to finance_team@company.com with subject "Financial Health Report" summarizing the findings and mentioning the Excel file and Notion page you created.

When you are done, call claim_done.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent and dispatch no sub-agent. The entire source is ten compact financial-statement calls for five fixed symbols, and the workbook, page, and email all use one canonical ten-value table.

Resolve the workspace dynamically. In one native-parallel response call `get_financial_statement` for `AMZN`, `GOOGL`, `JNJ`, `JPM`, and `XOM` with `financial_type="income_stmt"`, and in the same response call it once per symbol with `financial_type="balance_sheet"`. From each result choose the most recent annual period consistently across that statement, preserving the returned period label and exact fields for Total Revenue, Net Income, Total Assets, Total Liabilities, and Stockholders Equity. Do not substitute quarterly statements or mix periods. Freeze one symbol-keyed table and compute Profit_Margin_Pct once from unrounded revenue/income; treat a zero or missing denominator as a reported source gap rather than inventing a value.

The main agent is the sole writer of `Financial_Health_Report.xlsx` and the exact-title `Financial Health Dashboard` page. Create the workbook once with the exact two sheets, five alphabetically sorted rows apiece, exact headers, one-decimal profit margins, and literal numeric values; read both sheets back. Exhaust `API-post-search(query="Financial Health Dashboard")` and filter locally to exact titles. On zero exact matches, call `API-post-page` at most once with the complete legal envelope `parent={"workspace":true}`, `properties={"title":{"title":[{"type":"text","text":{"content":"Financial Health Dashboard"}}]}}`, and body `children`; never retry an ambiguous create or place the rich-text array directly under `properties.title`. On one exact match, retain and retrieve that page; on multiple exact matches, block instead of selecting arbitrarily. For the retained page, use `API-patch-page` only for missing/wrong properties and `API-patch-block-children` on its page ID to append missing body blocks. The body must name the verified highest-revenue company, best profit margin, and strongest balance sheet using one stated evidence-based measure consistently. After create/update, search the exact title again, require exactly one match with the retained ID, retrieve it, and read back both title and body. Only after both artifacts agree with the frozen table, check Sent mail and send one missing exact-recipient/subject email mentioning both deliverables and the canonical findings. Read back the sent record, call `claim_done`, and do not add a validation wave.

nodes.text:
You are a financial data gatherer. Use the Yahoo Finance tools (mcp__yahoo-finance__get_financial_statement) to retrieve the MOST RECENT ANNUAL financial statement data for five tracked stocks: AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM, XOM.

For EACH of the five tickers, retrieve:
1. Income statement (use financial_type = "income_stmt"): extract Total Revenue and Net Income. Net Income is typically labeled "Net Income" or "Net Income Common Stockholders". Total Revenue is typically "Total Revenue" or "Operating Revenue".
2. Balance sheet (use financial_type = "balance_sheet"): extract Total Assets, Total Liabilities, and Stockholders Equity. Stockholders Equity is typically labeled "Stockholders Equity" or "Total Stockholder Equity". Total Liabilities may be labeled "Total Liabilities" and can also be computed as Total Assets - Stockholders Equity if a direct figure is unavailable.

Do this for all five tickers. Note: use the annual (non-quarterly) statement types. The "most recent annual period" is the latest full fiscal year with data.

Return your result as a concise structured report. For each ticker, list:
- Symbol
- Total_Revenue (annual)
- Net_Income (annual)
- Total_Assets (annual)
- Total_Liabilities (annual)
- Stockholders_Equity (annual)

Use exact numeric values exactly as returned by Yahoo Finance. If a figure is reported in millions or in raw dollars, state the raw number you extracted so the numbers are directly usable. If any value is missing, note that clearly. Do not round or transform the values — just report the raw figures you find. Keep the report factual and complete.
Gather Yahoo Finance financial data

Create an Excel file at this exact path: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_claude-sonnet-5/SingleUserTurn-yf-financial-health-excel-notion/workspace/Financial_Health_Report.xlsx

The workbook must contain exactly two worksheets.

SHEET 1 — name it exactly "Income Statement". Header row (row 1): Symbol, Total_Revenue, Net_Income, Profit_Margin_Pct. Then 5 data rows, sorted alphabetically by Symbol (AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM, XOM). The Total_Revenue and Net_Income columns must hold the raw dollar values as integers, and Profit_Margin_Pct must hold the value already computed as Net_Income / Total_Revenue * 100 rounded to 1 decimal place. Data:

Row2: AMZN | 716924000000 | 77670000000 | 10.8
Row3: GOOGL | 402836000000 | 132170000000 | 32.8
Row4: JNJ | 94193000000 | 26804000000 | 28.5
Row5: JPM | 181847000000 | 57048000000 | 31.4
Row6: XOM | 323905000000 | 28844000000 | 8.9

SHEET 2 — name it exactly "Balance Sheet". Header row (row 1): Symbol, Total_Assets, Total_Liabilities, Equity. Then 5 data rows sorted alphabetically by Symbol. All values raw dollar integers. Data:

Row2: AMZN | 818042000000 | 406977000000 | 411065000000
Row3: GOOGL | 595281000000 | 180016000000 | 415265000000
Row4: JNJ | 199210000000 | 117666000000 | 81544000000
Row5: JPM | 4424900000000 | 4062462000000 | 362438000000
Row6: XOM | 448980000000 | 182354000000 | 259386000000

Make sure the values are stored as numbers (not text). Remove any default sheet that is not one of these two (e.g. if a "Sheet" is created by default, rename it to "Income Statement" and create "Balance Sheet", or delete the default after populating). After writing the file, verify by reading back both sheets and confirming the exact header order, exact symbols, exact numeric values, and alphabetically sorted rows. Report back the final file path and a confirmation that both sheets are correctly populated with all 5 rows each.
Build Financial_Health_Report.xlsx

Create a Notion page titled exactly "Financial Health Dashboard". Use the Notion API tool mcp__notion__API-post-page.

The page should be a parent-less page (created via post-search/post-page with appropriate parent, e.g. the shared/root location is fine — use the default parent that the API accepts, commonly a page_id of the workspace root). Provide a title "Financial Health Dashboard" and add paragraph/heading content summarizing the key findings from a financial health analysis of five companies (Amazon AMZN, Alphabet GOOGL, Johnson & Johnson JNJ, JPMorgan Chase JPM, ExxonMobil XOM), using FY2025 annual data:

- Highest revenue: AMZN with $716.9B total revenue (well ahead of GOOGL at $402.8B and XOM at $323.9B).
- Best profit margin: GOOGL with a net profit margin of ~32.8%, followed by JPM at 31.4% and JNJ at 28.5%. The weakest margins are XOM (~8.9%) and AMZN (~10.8%).
- Strongest balance sheets: GOOGL (equity $415.3B, assets $595.3B, liabilities $180.0B) and JPM (largest balance sheet overall with $4.42T in assets, equity $362.4B). XOM has strong equity ($259.4B) against $182.4B liabilities. JNJ has a comparatively smaller balance sheet ($199.2B assets, $81.5B equity). Note balance-sheet strength judged by absolute equity and the assets-to-liabilities cushion.

The page content should be well-structured (a heading plus bulleted list or paragraphs). After creating the page, retrieve it via API-retrieve-a-page to confirm it exists with the correct title. Report back the final page URL and page ID, and confirm the title is exactly "Financial Health Dashboard".
Create Notion Financial Health Dashboard
